verdict.rationale: Evidence only shows Airbyte exposing an MCP server so external agents (Claude, Cursor, etc.) can connect to Airbyte's data — i.e., Airbyte acts as the MCP server/tool provider, not as an MCP client consuming other MCP servers' tools. There is no documentation of Airbyte itself plugging in external MCP servers to use their tools. Missing for 10: any first-party or community evidence of Airbyte acting as an MCP client, configuration for adding external MCP servers, or a workflow where Airbyte consumes third-party MCP tools.
